title: Laura Pausini's World Tour arrives in Florence: "Music is the queen, and I am here to defend her"
text: Laura Pausini's World Tour arrives in Florence: “Music is the queen, and I am here to defend her” On 6 and 7 November, the Italian superstar brings her spectacular live show to the Mandela Forum. Expect career-defining hits, lesser-known gems and a striking stage production. Twenty years have passed since Laura Pausini made history by filling Milan's San Siro Stadium, becoming the first female artist ever to do so and bringing thousands of fans together in what felt like a celebratory ritual. Io Canto — Yo Canto World Tour 2026\/27 , which has already sold a remarkable 450,000 tickets. The tour kicked off in Pamplona last March before marking its way across the Americas and now brings Pausini to Florence's Nelson Mandela Forum on 6 and 7 November. Laura Pausini performs during a concert at the Movistar Arena in Madrid, Spain, on 6 April 2026.The singer is on her Io Canto \/ Yo Canto World Tour 2026\/2027, which began in Pamplona, Spain, on 27 March. Photo: Ricardo Rubio\/Europa Press via Getty Images “This year, the tour opened in Spain, South America and the United States. Three uninterrupted months on the road, travelling around the world, gave me an incredible boost of energy,” Pausini says.“I couldn't wait to bring this show, which means so much to me, to Europe and, above all, to Italy. If it were up to me, I would live on stage. It's my natural habitat, and being close to my audience and reconnecting with them live, year after year, is an absolute necessity for me. ”Laura Pausini on the final night of the 76th Sanremo Music Festival in Sanremo, Italy, on 28 February 2026.Photo: Pool Insabato Rovaris\/Mondadori Portfolio via Getty Images The setlist will bring together some of the biggest hits from a career that officially began on 27 February 1993, when a young Pausini won the Sanremo Music Festival withThese are songs that have become part of the collective memory, thanks to their ability to mirror emotions and experiences that resonate with people's everyday lives. Perhaps this powerful sense of connection is one of the reasons why Pausini is the most-streamed female Italian artist in the world.One of the concert's highlights will be a medley paying tribute to fellow Italian artists, including Renato Zero, Gino Paoli, Umberto Tozzi and Ornella Vanoni. Joining Laura on stage will be a seven-piece band and five backing vocalists, under the musical direction of Paolo Carta. This marks his eighth time taking on the role for one of the singer's world tours.“Putting the setlist together means respecting the balance of my repertoire while following the story of my career in every country that has accompanied me over the years,” explains the artist, who has sold more than 75 million records worldwide and amassed over eight billion streams. “The European leg features many of my greatest hits, but also plenty of songs that may be less familiar to the general public but are much loved by my fans.These are the tracks they ask me to perform, and I love alternating them throughout the show. ”Nicole Scherzinger, Robbie Williams and Laura Pausini perform before the 2026 FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina at New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on 19 July 2026. Photo: Justin Setterfield\/Getty Images , her tribute album celebrating the artists and songwriters who have shaped Italian music history, released last March.The Spanish-language edition of the project, dedicated to Latin American singer-songwriters, has recently earned Pausini her 12th Latin Grammy nomination. ). The nomination comes three years after the Latin Recording Academy named her 2023 Latin Grammy Person of the Year, making her the first and only non-native Spanish-speaking artist to receive the honour. Her connection with South America, after all, has become an inseparable part of her artistic journey.“I'm thrilled by the affection and recognition that the Latin and American worlds have shown me for more than 30 years. Every time a nomination comes along, it feels different. You can never take it for granted. ”Luca Tommassini attends the Kinéo Award ceremony during the 83rd Venice International Film Festival in Venice, Italy, on 5 September 2026.Photo: Maya Cellixa\/Getty Images The stage production plays a central role in the show, conceived by Pausini together with her trusted creative collaborator Luca Tommasini. The underlying idea was to create a luminous fortress: a protective space for music, with Laura taking on the role of a warrior who defends it, celebrates it and shares it with her audience. All materials used for the special effects are environmentally sustainable.The entire show, organised and produced by Friends&Partners, has been meticulously planned to give each segment its own significance.“The stage is our land, our fortress. The microphone stand is an extension of my muscles and of my voice. The microphone is my challenge, your voice, our megaphone. In this castle, I am not the queen: music is the queen, and I am here to defend her,” the singer declares at the opening of the show.Diane Warren and Laura Pausini attend the 93rd Academy Awards at Union Station in Los Angeles, California, on 25 April 2021. Photo: Richard Harbaugh\/A.M.P. A.S. via Getty Images As she has done throughout her career, Pausini is also using this tour to keep the spotlight on violence against women. A longtime supporter of the Una Nessuna Centomila foundation, she has dedicated a special segment of the show to the issue, centred on“Violence is a silent scream disguised as love.It feeds on silence and leaves broken wings behind. It can only be defeated when no one is left invisible,” she says.
